methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: EPA grant backs community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: EPA-funded community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia signals grassroots capacity-building in an historically underserved region, potentially distributing AI-adjacent skills through local networks rather than centralized platforms.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: AI pressure on Richmond's young workforce suggests platform-delivered automation creating shallow, widespread displacement rather than deep capability development, concentrating control in tools rather than human expertise.

signals.title: Pentagon Expands Scale AI Deal to $500M and AI Defense Firm TurbineOne Moves HQ to Northern Virginia - Clearance Jobs
signals.signal_reading: Pentagon's $500M AI deal expansion and TurbineOne HQ relocation to NoVA reinforces the region's defense-AI talent concentration, deepening the capability gap between metro hubs and the rest of Virginia.

signals.title: Hampton Roads taking steps to prepare for data centers - The Virginian-Pilot
signals.signal_reading: Hampton Roads preparing for data centers signals infrastructure-led concentration in a second metro hub, but without explicit workforce development suggests shallow platform adoption rather than distributed AI literacy.

signals.title: RC-RV partners with ed2go to launch innovative, on-demand workforce training programs - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's partnership with ed2go for on-demand training platforms represents outsourced, commodified skill delivery rather than locally-developed AI expertise, distributing access but not depth of capability.
